SOURCE B: docs/MILESTONE-VALIDATION.md, the milestone requirements of the audit
SOURCE C: LESSON-PREFLIGHT.json, the lessons the engineering memory imposes

requirements.description: A canonical, machine-readable requirement specification exists for this Gate and the registry mirrors it row for row.
The derived expected set names the specification of the Gate it describes instead of a fixed document.
The delivery-assurance scope covers the runtime source this Gate introduces, so a gate result becomes stale when the product changes.
The closed mandatory gate registry carries every executable gate this Gate introduces.
Every test suite this Gate introduces is declared canonically and is counted by the count derivation and resolvable as evidence.
The internal mirror audit judges the Gate it runs in rather than a Gate named in its own source.
The internal Red Team battery of this Gate is executable, scoped to the Foundation, and records a null-mutation control.
The repository carries the planned application, service, package and infrastructure directories.
A directory reserved for a later Gate says so and contains no implementation.
No later-Gate capability is implemented, simulated or faked in this Gate.
The backend is a real FastAPI application that starts reliably and fails loudly when it cannot.
Shutdown is graceful and releases every client the application opened.
Dependency lifecycle is explicit and held on the application, not in ambient mutable globals.
`GET /health` reports process liveness and does not depend on external dependencies to answer.
`GET /ready` probes PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO and Temporal and refuses readiness when a mandatory dependency is unavailable.
`GET /version` reports the application version and build identity and exposes no secret.
The application exposes a Prometheus metrics endpoint with request, latency, status and dependency metrics.
OpenAPI documentation describes the Foundation endpoints and exposes no internal-only route.
CORS is configured explicitly from configuration, without a permissive wildcard, and allows the local frontend.
Configuration is typed, validated at load time and rejects an invalid or missing mandatory value.
Safe defaults, development configuration and test configuration are separated rather than conflated.
A committed example environment file documents every key and carries no real secret, and the real file is ignored by Git.
Secret values are redacted wherever configuration, errors or logs could expose them.
No secret is baked into an image, a compose file, a Dockerfile or a committed configuration file.
PostgreSQL runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version with a persistent named volume.
The persistence layer is real, asynchronous and pooled, built on SQLAlchemy 2.
Alembic migrations run from zero against an empty database and produce the declared schema.
Starting against an already-migrated database neither fails nor recreates the schema.
A failed migration never produces a healthy readiness or a silent partial start.
The structural domain tables the later Gates build on exist, with their relationships and constraints.
Identifiers use one consistent strategy, UUIDv7, implemented and tested rather than assumed.
The common column convention is defined once and applied where it makes sense, not forced everywhere.
The pgvector position is decided, recorded, and — where the extension is enabled — migrated and tested.
Redis runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version.
The backend holds a real Redis client whose availability the readiness probe verifies.
An integration test exercises a real Redis round trip against the running service.
MinIO runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version with a persistent named volume.
The buckets the later Gates need are created by an idempotent bootstrap that is safe to re-run.
The readiness probe verifies real object-storage connectivity rather than a reachable port.
An integration test writes, reads and deletes a real object.
Temporal runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version with its persistent state.
An IACode worker connects to Temporal and polls its task queue as a first-class service.
The readiness probe verifies real Temporal connectivity.
A minimal real workflow and activity execute end to end through the worker and return an observable result.
No agent workflow, tool call or orchestration of a later Gate is implemented here.
A real Angular application exists and builds reproducibly with pinned dependencies.
The Foundation page identifies IACode and renders the live backend health, readiness and version.
The API base address is centralized in configuration, carries no secret and is not hardcoded across the code.
Frontend unit tests run headless and are part of the verification command.
Every image builds from a pinned base, runs as a non-root user where practical, carries no secret and excludes build waste.
The compose stack declares every Foundation service and nothing that the Foundation does not need.
Every service that can report health has a real healthcheck, and start-up ordering uses those conditions instead of fixed sleeps.
Restart behaviour is declared, and the stack recovers its state after a restart.
Durable state lives in named volumes that are documented, not in the container filesystem.
The stack uses an explicit network and publishes only the ports local development needs, from configuration.
The backend and the worker emit structured logs carrying the contract fields, absent rather than invented when there is no context.
Every HTTP request carries a correlation identifier that is accepted or generated, propagated, returned and logged.
The API error contract is explicit, extensible and never returns a traceback or internal detail to the client while keeping it in the logs.
Prometheus is provisioned and scrapes the API and the worker.
Grafana starts with the Prometheus datasource and a Foundation dashboard provisioned automatically.
The OpenTelemetry position for the Foundation is decided and recorded rather than left implicit.
A reproducible backup produces a PostgreSQL dump and the object-storage contents, with a correct exit code and a log, and fails loudly on partial failure.
The backup never writes a credential into its artifacts or its log.
A restore reconstructs the database and the object storage from a backup produced by this tooling.
Backup and restore are verified end to end with synthetic data in a disposable environment, and the restored data is checked rather than assumed.
Backup retention for the Foundation is either implemented simply or documented as out of scope, with no silent gap.
One documented command runs the whole Gate verification and works on the primary Windows environment as well as on POSIX.
The backend suite covers health, readiness, version, configuration, redaction, error handling, correlation, database, cache, object storage, workflows and migrations.
The frontend suite covers bootstrap, the status rendering and the API configuration, and the production build succeeds.
Infrastructure smoke validation proves that our own configuration of each service is operational.
A fresh installation with no previous volume reaches a ready stack, a migrated database, a reachable frontend and a green smoke check.
A restart of the running stack returns every service to ready with its data intact.
With a mandatory dependency stopped, liveness may stay up while readiness fails correctly, and readiness recovers when the dependency returns.
Lint and static analysis run over the backend, the worker and the frontend and are green.
A dependency vulnerability scan is executed, or its absence is justified, and relevant Critical and High findings block the Gate.
The repository entry documentation describes what exists after this Gate and how to run it.
The architecture document describes the Foundation runtime, its boundaries and what is deliberately absent.
A development guide explains the local workflow end to end for a new machine.
An operational runbook documents start, stop, rebuild, reset, migrate, health, readiness, Grafana and the smoke checks.
A backup and restore runbook documents the full procedure and its verification.
The pinned versions of every runtime, service and principal library are recorded in one place.
Every structural decision of this Gate that is not already recorded becomes an ADR, and no ADR duplicates an existing decision.
The entry contract and the plan describe the current Gate and its status truthfully.
The Gate produces a retrospective from the canonical template.
Verify checkpoint validation must succeed from a detached checkout of the checkpoint tag
Verify a file inventory must be recomputed from the repository, never trusted as an assertion
Verify every operation attempt must be auditable, including a refusal decided before execution
Verify a checkpoint may never claim readiness while it also claims to be blocked
Verify a PASS requires evidence that can be executed or resolved, not a statement
Verify the repository must be self-contained; a specification may not live outside it
Verify independent validation cannot be declared by the run that did the work
Verify requirement completeness must be total and evidence-backed before handoff
Verify a red gate requires rework, never a waiver, and never a weakened check
Verify a recorded command must carry runtime, working directory, commit and purpose to be replayable
Verify a control over a checkpoint's own evidence must be scoped to the moment it matters
Verify sealed checkpoints and their tags are immutable, and tooling must keep validating them
Verify an installed capability must be detected by resolved path, not by a bare command lookup
Verify evidence must be recorded as it happens, not reconstructed at the end of a run
Verify every positive terminal status needs one shared promotion invariant
Verify a mandatory set must be closed by policy, never chosen by the caller
Verify a completeness denominator must come from a source the delivery does not own
Verify a structured reference must be resolved, not merely well typed
Verify a derived artifact must carry a fingerprint of the inputs that produced it
Verify evidence produced from a dirty tree needs immutable input identity
Verify sealed history needs an anchor outside the content it describes
Verify an authoritative count must be derived once, never maintained by hand twice
Verify a lesson must cite a source that actually records the finding it claims
Verify a control is finished only when its positive path has been executed, not only its refusals
Verify a generic guardrail derives repository state instead of naming today's checkpoint
Verify an adversarial battery without a null-mutation control proves nothing
Verify a lesson's prose may record a residual limit but may never contradict its status
Verify a configuration key that no code reads is a defect, not documentation
Verify a required protocol transition must never turn a mandatory gate red
Verify an empty applicable set is not a missing required set, and a control must tell them apart
Verify a control written while one Gate was the only Gate stops being a control when the next one starts
Verify a value bound in middleware is absent in the handlers that run outside it
Verify re-deriving what the framework already computed diverges from the framework
Verify captured subprocess output decoded or re-emitted with the platform codepage crashes the tool, not the work
